newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso recovers, ends firm after calm trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso recovers, ends firm after calm trade.

text.p: The Mexican peso reversed early weakness to close a little firmer on Monday due to a lack of dollar buyers in a quiet market, traders said.
"Some dealers stepped in to buy dollars early on after they had invested in peso instruments over the weekend," a trader said. "Then the peso recovered as few dealers bought dollars thereafter."
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart were 0.3 and 0.5 of a centavo firmer, at 7.8920/7.8980 and 7.8830/7.8880 per dollar respectively.
The same-day peso closed earlier 0.8 of a centavo weaker at 7.8900/7.8950 per dollar.

Traders said dealing was light during the session as the market awaited the outcome of the primary Cetes auction later in the day and the possibility of dealers exercising dollar puts bought from the central bank.
The central bank brought forward the Cetes auction to Monday as the working week will be shortened by Wednesday's holiday to commemorate the anniversary of the Mexican Revolution.
A Reuters survey of money market dealers showed they expected Banco de Mexico to assign bellwether 28-day Cetes at 29.87 percent, or two basis points below last week's auction rate.
Traders said that if the auction turned out as forecast, the change would be so small as to have no effect on peso trading on Tuesday.
